issue.title: [distributed, model] feat: add hybrid sequence parallelism for qwen4 exp

repository.name: VeOmni
repository.description: VeOmni: Scaling Any Modality Model Training with Model-Centric Distributed Recipe Zoo

issue.body:
Add opt-in hybrid Ulysses/context parallelism for Qwen4-Exp long-context training. Inputs remain sequence-local; QSA exchanges heads within Ulysses and gathers global KV across CP. Compact selections retain global token coordinates. GDN exchanges the combined SP sequence for local heads; PLE exchanges packed-aware halos.

The current upstream mesh is CP-major/Ulysses-inner (`[CP,U]`). KV all-gather already produces canonical token order, so no CP/U axis transpose is applied. The model factory permits Qwen4 U8CP2/U8CP4 only with explicit opt-in, and rejects the hybrid opt-in for other models. Existing U1 GPU-native CP remains supported. Cache decoding, explicit CP attention masks and training attention dropout fail closed.

Dependency: #1231 supplies the bounded CANN QSA kernel. All three kernel source files here match its exact `7d4cdbc8` contents, including INT8 mask scatter; merge #1231 first. Retain its native kernel tests/workflow invocation. #1275 is the separate NPU TopK follow-up. #1087 is not a dependency of this model path.

Memory limits: GDN remains headwise and processes the full sequence per local head; QSA gathers global KV. This is not ring attention and does not promise proportional whole-model memory savings as CP increases.

Validation after current-main integration (`6438cbe3`):

- Reproduced the old token-order failure with a real 4-rank Gloo launch, then corrected the patch configuration and regenerated both GPU/NPU modules with Transformers 5.16.1.
- Four collected Gloo gates passed: U2CP2/U2CP4, both generated variants, packed boundaries across CP edges, output/input/all parameter gradients, PLE/GDN independent segments, full toy text model and non-reentrant checkpointing. GDN device kernels use deterministic CPU references.
- 19 CPU factory/parallel-state/import-isolation checks and Gloo variants passed; the factory regressions and Gloo gates are enumerated in both hardware workflows.
- All-model `patchgen --check`, pinned Ruff 0.13.2 and whitespace checks passed; independent review safe.

Native GPU/NPU kernels, production U8 geometry, FSDP/EP, multimodal distributed training, cold DCP resume and performance remain separate qualification gates. This is peer-review Candidate, not a newly Verified/Released training profile.

Final test-collection follow-up: `5ecf2d601` defers the standalone MoE shim and generated-model imports until script execution. A collection regression asserts the existing MoE package object remains unchanged. The composed stack repeated all 19 CP/factory/import-isolation checks successfully. Production sources are unchanged by this follow-up.

### Current-main synchronization — 2026-10-13

Published `28142693ac5012d05907af718387710324fa5ce3` integrates upstream main `0832477680a5a9f8f4209211d6110cdb199dd086` with a normal merge. Pinned Ruff 0.13.2 quality and whitespace checks passed; independent review safe. Native accelerator qualification is still a separate gate.

The ParallelPlan resolution preserves persistent SP opt-in validation and upstream complete parameter-owner discovery/nested-owner rejection. Generated Qwen4 files match the prior PR head. All-model patchgen drift passes using the current worktree’s patchgen package. #1231 remains the kernel dependency.

### Maintainer repair — 2026-10-16

Normally merged upstream main plus repaired #1223 and #1231, retaining CUDA TileLang, CANN QSA and native CI gates. Preserve explicit non-CP dictionary masks through index selection and attention; reject unsupported CP masks at the text-model boundary before collectives. Restrict the remote-halo width guard to distributed calls, restoring one-token non-SP tails. Updated PLE packed-length signatures and consolidated native Ulysses fixtures. Preserve TileLang dropout fallback and checkpoint RNG state. **36 portable/distributed checks passed, 65 native checks skipped**, including real U2CP2/U2CP4 for both generated variants, packed boundaries, full toy-model output/input/all-parameter gradients and recomputation. All-model patchgen drift (Transformers 5.16.1), Ruff 0.13.2 and independent review passed.

Published revision: `05549b739e16bd1afc8f313613f69ac240a77002`. No force push or training JobRun modification.

Registry migration remains conditional on upstream #1142 landing. That breaking refactor is still open; these revisions target the current public-main dispatch API and do not claim compatibility with an unmerged future API.

### Native feedback dependency correction — 2026-10-16

The previous requested revision 05549b739 did not include the later native masked-row correction. This revision normally merges #1231 bcd8820d3 and latest upstream 0c1d90866, plus standalone norm dependency 0df941853. Fully masked outputs/dQ are explicitly zero; zero incoming gradients do not contaminate an empty batch item's dK/dV. Existing exact-zero assertions and native numerical tolerances are retained. Targeted portable/Gloo/current-ParallelState checks:51passed,9native skipped. All generated files pass drift and are unchanged by the kernel correction; independent review safe.

Current exact revision: `4449a5e0fb4504cd268affa9daea4e8185b3097a`. No forced history rewrite, resource action or new native success claim.

### Vision dummy synchronization — 2026-10-17

Public revision: `a7ef3e23e`. Synchronizes the narrow vision-dummy correction already used by the runtime integration; no other composition changes are imported. Qwen4-Exp's unsharded vision tower consumes a global patch grid, so text-only dummy inputs and varlen metadata now contain the complete grid rather than only 1/SP of its rows. This fixes the 4-patch versus 64-position mismatch under U8CP2.

Regenerated both GPU/NPU modeling files and checked-in diff artifacts using Transformers 5.16.1. A fresh-process, real vision forward/backward regression covers both generated variants and simulated SP sizes 1/2/8/16/32, matching explicit global-grid inputs exactly; all 10 cases passed. It is enumerated in both unit workflows and costs about 12 seconds locally. The test exercises CPU arithmetic and simulated geometry, not distributed accelerator execution. An additional 19 factory/import-isolation/real CPU-Gloo checks passed (U2CP2/U2CP4, both variants). All-model patchgen drift, pinned Ruff and independent review passed.

The compact-layout and packed-length caching performance suggestions remain unimplemented and are tracked separately. Complete native checkpoint/cold-resume qualification remains a separate gate; no new Verified/Released profile is claimed.

### Packed metadata optimization — 2026-10-18

Revision `0d5bcd0aa2d9c1eac08458c4b5f7e6ed861c2d08` addresses both metadata-performance review findings. Resolve validated main and independent GDN packed lengths once per forward; reuse a content/topology/device-keyed integer-only QSA layout across layers and checkpoint recomputation. Stable owner-major ordering, packed sample isolation, halos, tails and empty-owner gradient dependencies are retained. Compressed-row gather accepts host counts and cached crop indices, while existing tensor-count callers keep their interface. No changes to projection, score, TopK or attention arithmetic, optimizer precision or training geometry.

Validation on this public revision: 41 CPU/real-Gloo checks passed, including layout invalidation, independent GDN boundaries, both generated model variants at U2CP2/U2CP4, multi-layer/checkpoint reuse and vision dummy. Another 15 shared CP sharding checks passed. GPU/NPU .py and .diff were generated with Transformers 5.16.1; all-model drift, Ruff 0.13.2, whitespace and independent review passed. GPU already collects the layout test directory; NPU explicitly enumerates the new portable test. The opt-in native replay references the public #1275 baseline and requires that NPU-safe TopK follow-up in both baseline and candidate.

Integration evidence (composed with #1275): a 32-Ascend training comparison completed 9 optimizer steps, comparing the same steps 2–9 after excluding startup. Mean elapsed step time decreased from 1454.00 s to 1413.75 s, a 2.85% nominal throughput increase (GBS64 × 131072 capacity: 0.4985B → 0.5127B token/day). This is a modest metadata/synchronization improvement, not a new attention-compute speedup. Native indices and small forward/backward comparisons passed in that integration; full-training loss/gradients remained finite. These integration results do not establish full-model bitwise/update equivalence, statistical convergence, DCP save or fresh-process cold resume. The overall training profile remains Candidate.

issue.title: [model] fix: avoid infinite masked QSA TopK scores on NPU

repository.name: VeOmni
repository.description: VeOmni: Scaling Any Modality Model Training with Model-Centric Distributed Recipe Zoo

issue.body:
### What does this PR do?

Avoid a reproducible Ascend 910B2/CANN 9 TopKV2 AICore failure in the batched, packed Qwen4-Exp QSA indexer. Sparse rows containing many masked `-inf` scores can raise error 507015 (`VEC supports illegal configurations`), including full query chunks.

On NPU only, mask invisible block scores with `-1.0` instead of `-inf`. QSA computes `ReLU(scores).sum(...) / sqrt(head_dim)`, so finite visible scores are nonnegative, including exact zeros. The finite sentinel remains strictly below every valid score. The existing `visible.gather` filter discards masked selections when a row has fewer than `k` visible blocks or is fully masked. CPU/CUDA behavior is unchanged.

### Current-main rebase after #1142

Rebased as a standalone one-commit change onto public `main` after the breaking `OpSlot -> VeomniOp` registry migration (#1142). The device-specific substitution targets the model-owned `Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer.forward` selection in patchgen; the registered `qsa_attention` kernel rows and their `(op, variant, impl, device)` identities are unchanged. No `veomni/ops/kernels/qwen4_exp/npu_qsa.py` module exists on the current base.

Scope is four files: the NPU patch config, its generated NPU source/diff, and the selector regression.

### Validation

- Rebased onto `main@cbae2416782eccf3f1bf9be9bfb49ff9db1aec14`.
- `pytest -q tests/models/test_qwen4_exp_qsa_topk.py`: **7 passed, 6 native NPU cases skipped**.
- Full repository `patchgen --check`: all generated files up to date, including `qwen4_exp_gpu` and `qwen4_exp_npu`.
- Targeted Ruff check/format and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Earlier isolated Ascend 910B2/CANN9 validation reproduced the `-inf` baseline device failure and completed with finite `-1`; native accelerator CI remains the required fresh gate.

No training JobRun was modified.

body:
Heads-up on ordering: #1142 (`[BREAKING][ops, model] refactor: replace OpSlot with VeomniOp`) is planned to land before this PR, so please rebase onto `main` after it merges and build the kernel changes here on the new op registry.

What changes in #1142:
- `OpSlot` / `OpsConfigSlot` / `KERNEL_REGISTRY` / `KernelSpec` (`veomni.ops.dispatch`, `veomni.ops.kernel_registry`) are removed.
- Every kernel is a row registered with `register_op(op, variant, impl, ..., requirement=..., requires=(...))`, keyed by `(op, variant, impl, device)`. The device is chosen with `GpuKernelRequirement` / `NpuKernelRequirement` / `MluKernelRequirement`.
- Modeling code holds a handle: `VeomniOp(op, variant, resolve_op_impl("<field>_implementation"))`. It does not read config fields or bind slots.
- Kernels live under `veomni/ops/kernels/<op>/<variant>/<impl>.py`, with the rows in `veomni/ops/kernels/<op>/__init__.py`. Many files moved.

How to register and call an op: [`veomni/ops/README.md` → Registering an op](https://github.com/Zx55/VeOmni/blob/czr/kernel-registry-refactor/veomni/ops/README.md#registering-an-op) and [Calling an op from modeling](https://github.com/Zx55/VeOmni/blob/czr/kernel-registry-refactor/veomni/ops/README.md#calling-an-op-from-modeling); config fields and available impls: [`docs/design/op_selection.md`](https://github.com/Zx55/VeOmni/blob/czr/kernel-registry-refactor/docs/design/op_selection.md).

For this PR specifically:
- `veomni/ops/kernels/qwen4_exp/npu_qsa.py` should become registered rows of a QSA op (NPU row with `NpuKernelRequirement()`, plus an eager reference row) instead of a module the patch_gen imports directly.
- The qwen4_exp patch_gen configs now call ops through `VeomniOp`, so select the QSA impl the same way, and re-run `make patchgen` after rebasing.

issue.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds a selector-index Triton QSA fast path for Qwen4-Exp CUDA attention. It preserves the model's selector-selected-token semantics rather than substituting dense FlashAttention, while retaining the upstream eager/SDPA implementation whenever the fast-path contract is not satisfied.

### Checklist Before Starting

- Search for relative PRs/issues and link here: builds on the Qwen4-Exp support merged in #1151.
- PR title follows the required `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` format.

### Test

- Regenerated Qwen4-Exp GPU and NPU patchgen outputs from the public `main` baseline and ran `patchgen --check`: all 31 patch configurations passed.
- Added `tests/ops/test_qwen4_exp_qsa.py`. GPU CI runs all `tests/ops/`; the suite compares QSA forward and backward against sparse eager gather for T=64/128, GQA and non-GQA, selector-tail capacity, and padding behavior.
- Local CPU environment has no CUDA/Triton execution path, so the focused suite reports 7 expected skips.
- Accepted H100 validation used the same sparse eager oracle: output/dQ/dK/dV relative errors were all below 1e-2; F+B improved from 88.66 ms to 55.64 ms (1.593x).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` on changed files, and `git diff --check` passed. `make quality` reaches ruff successfully but fails format checking on 25 pre-existing unrelated docs/tests on public `main`.

### API and Usage Example

No user-facing API change. Qwen4-Exp GPU attention automatically uses QSA when CUDA tensors meet the kernel contract. CPU, NPU, cached decoding, attention-weight requests, nonzero training dropout, unavailable Triton, and unsupported layouts retain eager/SDPA behavior.

### Design & Code Changes

- Add a Qwen4-Exp-specific Triton QSA kernel supporting forward/backward, GQA and non-GQA, and selector tail blocks.
- Expose selector-produced indices and counts to the CUDA QSA path without reconstructing them from a dense mask.
- Preserve sentinel-aware dense-mask construction for eager/SDPA fallback.
- Gate QSA after Q/K/V/RoPE construction with a concrete tensor contract; unsupported inputs safely fall back.
- Keep the NPU patch configuration on the upstream eager/SDPA path and remove CUDA QSA imports/overrides from its generated output.
- Regenerate patchgen outputs and document the dispatch contract.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Applied focused ruff and patchgen checks.
- [x] Added/updated documentation.
- [x] Added a GPU CI-enumerated kernel test.
- [x] Ran independent code review; verdict: safe.
